concepts.title: Reading Large Numbers: Lakh and Crore

questions.q: Fermat's Last Theorem says x^n + y^n = z^n has no positive solutions for n > 2. For n = 3 compute 5^3 - (3^3 + 4^3) to see it is not zero.
Check whether 6 is a perfect number: its proper divisors are 1, 2 and 3. Find their sum.
The numbers 11 and 13 are consecutive primes. How far apart are they (twin primes differ by 2)?
Are 8 and 15 co-prime? Their common factors are only 1, so their HCF is what?
Divisibility by 9: a number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is. Find the digit sum of 729 and report the digit sum.
Divisibility by 11: add and subtract alternate digits of 2728 from the right (8 - 2 + 7 - 2) and report the result.
Evaluate 3x + 2 when x = 2.
Find the value of 3x^2 + 7x + 5 when x = 3.
Simplify 4x + 7x - 6x and give the coefficient of x.
Use the distributive law: 7 x (5 + 3) equals 7 x 5 + 7 x 3. Compute it.
Evaluate 4 + 3 x 9 (respect the order of operations).
Evaluate (7 + 3) x 7.
